Change c0502. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): August 26th, 17—.

1818 text: You have read this strange and terrific story, Margaret; and do you not feel your blood congealed with horror, like that which even now curdles mine? Sometimes, seized with sudden agony, he could not continue his tale; at others, his voice broken, yet piercing, uttered with difficulty the words so replete with agony.

1831 text: You have read this strange and terrific story, Margaret; and do you not feel your blood congeal with horror, like that which even now curdles mine? Sometimes, seized with sudden agony, he could not continue his tale; at others, his voice broken, yet piercing, uttered with difficulty the words so replete with anguish.

Diff: You have read this strange and terrific story, Margaret; and do you not feel your blood [-congealed-] {+congeal+} with horror, like that which even now curdles mine? Sometimes, seized with sudden agony, he could not continue his tale; at others, his voice broken, yet piercing, uttered with difficulty the words so replete with [-agony-] {+anguish+} .

Context after (unchanged): His fine and lovely eyes were now lighted up with indignation, now subdued to downcast sorrow, and quenched in infinite wretchedness.

result.rationale: Two small diction/grammar changes: "congealed" becomes "congeal" (verb form after "do you not feel your blood") and "replete with agony" becomes "anguish," which avoids repeating "agony" from the previous clause. Meaning is unchanged.
